title: Field-term dip vs firing rate as a marker of peak acceleration
question: Does the field-term dip mark peak acceleration better than firing rate, polarization indices, PCA/GPFA trajectories and decoders, and does the coupled model (M1) add anything over the independent model (M0)? How does our method deviate from standard methods?
headline: Field-term dip locks to peak acceleration (65% vs 14% rest control; 50 ms vs 330 ms for mean rate) but is a population-polarization effect: no detectable advantage of coupling-corrected fields (FT vs FT0, CIs wide) and a model-free polarization index matches it.
